newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers talks end in stalemate.
newsitem.headline: French truckers talks end in stalemate.

text.p: Marathon overnight talks between striking French truck drivers and employers ended in stalemate on Monday as protesters tightened their grip with blockades of towns, petrol depots and ports after a weekend pause.

Unions said talks with a state mediator ended with no results after almost 14 hours at the French Transport Ministry. Meanwhile, truckers bolstered their action, blockading the Channel port of Calais to lorries travelling by ferry to Britain.
"That was 14 hours for nothing," said Roger Poletti, a leader of the Force Ouvriere union after the meeting over the eight-day conflict squeezing the French economy.

Both sides agreed to meet for a new round of the talks, hosted by government mediator Robert Cros, at 5 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Monday in a bid to resolve the truckers' demands for shorter working hours, wage increases and retirement at age 55 instead of 60.

The truckers reinforced their campaign on Monday, with barricades at five frontier posts with Germany and blockades at the port of Calais and Boulogne-sur-mer, major routes for ferries to Britain. Cars and buses were allowed to embark on the ferries.

The truckers also blocked fuel depots and roads around the nation in the latest of a wave of union unrest in France. An IPSOS opinion poll for France-2 television showed that 74 percent of French people sympathised with the strikers' demands.
